item.title: Numeric in PostgreSQL
item.description:
How To Use NUMERIC in PostgreSQL

PostgreSQL provides the NUMERIC data type for storing numeric values with high precision. This article will guide you through the usage of the NUMERIC type for accurate numeric calculations.

Practical Example

-- Example: Using NUMERIC for precise calculations
SELECT CAST('123.456' AS NUMERIC) * 2 AS result;

In this example, we cast a string to the NUMERIC type and perform a multiplication operation.

FAQs on Using NUMERIC in PostgreSQL

Q: What is the advantage of using NUMERIC over other numeric types?

The NUMERIC type in PostgreSQL offers higher precision compared to other numeric types. It is suitable for scenarios where precision is crucial, such as financial calculations, where rounding errors need to be minimized.

Q: Can I perform mathematical operations with NUMERIC and other numeric types?

Yes, you can perform mathematical operations between NUMERIC and other numeric types. PostgreSQL will automatically convert between numeric types as needed for the operation.

item.title: Using INTERVAL in PostgreSQL
item.description:
How To Use INTERVAL in PostgreSQL

The INTERVAL data type in PostgreSQL allows you to store and manipulate periods of time. In this article, we’ll explore how to use INTERVAL in PostgreSQL for various time-related operations.

Practical Example

item.title: What is Trigger in SQL? 2023
item.description:
Trigger is a special type of stored procedure that is executed automatically in response to certain events on a database table Triggers are used to enforce business rules, maintain data integrity, and perform tasks such as auditing.

Triggers can be activated by various events, such as INSERT , UPDATE , DELETE , or SELECT statements on a table, or by direct invocation using the EXECUTE or CALL statement. Triggers can also be activated by database events such as logon, logoff, or server startup.
